69405-bolo-the-cave-boy.title: Bolo the Cave Boy
69405-bolo-the-cave-boy.creator: _Katherine Atherton Grimes_
69405-bolo-the-cave-boy.description: A book by _Katherine Atherton Grimes_. Bolo saw that Fisher had something in his hand. It was a long, stout cord of reindeer sinew, and on one end of it was tied a splinter of bone. The splinter was sharp at both ends and the cord was fastened to the middle of it.

75006-fair-play.title: _A Novel_
75006-fair-play.creator: Mrs. E. D. E. N. Southworth
75006-fair-play.description: A book by Mrs. E. D. E. N. Southworth. Four more beautiful young creatures than these could scarcely be found in the world. They were called the Four Belles of Bellemont. They would have been belles anywhere and borne off palms of beauty from all other competitors. Yet beautiful as each one was, the four were not rival belles; because, in fact, each one was of a totally different style from all the others.

arxiv-1502-01236.title: Estimating the Attack Ratio of Dengue Epidemics under Time-varying
arxiv-1502-01236.creator: Force of Infection using Aggregated Notification Data
arxiv-1502-01236.description:
A 2015 arXiv research paper by Force of Infection using Aggregated Notification Data. Abstract

Quantifying the attack ratio of disease is key to epidemiological inference and
Public Health planning. For multi-serotype pathogens, however, different levels of
serotype-specific immunity make it difficult to assess the population at risk. In this paper we propose a Bayesian method for estimation of the attack ratio
of an epidemic and the initial fraction of susceptibles using aggregated
incidence data.

arxiv-1712-00960.title: FSSD: Feature Fusion Single Shot Multibox Detector
arxiv-1712-00960.creator: Zuo-Xin Li Lu Yang Fu-Qiang Zhou
arxiv-1712-00960.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Zuo-Xin Li Lu Yang Fu-Qiang Zhou. SSD (Single Shot Multibox Detetor) is one of the best object detection algorithms with both high accuracy and fast speed. However, SSD’s feature pyramid detection method makes it hard to fuse the features from different scales. In this paper, we proposed FSSD (Feature Fusion Single Shot Multibox Detector), an enhanced SSD with a novel and lightweight feature fusion module which can improve the performance significantly over SSD with just a little speed drop.

arxiv-2002-08679.title: Neural Network Compression Framework for fast model inference
arxiv-2002-08679.creator: Alexander Kozlov, Ivan Lazarevich, Vasily Shamporov, Nikolay Lyalyushkin, Yury Gorbachev
arxiv-2002-08679.description: Abstract We present a new PyTorch-based framework for neural network compression with fine-tuning named Neural Network Compression Framework (NNCF) 1 1 1 Available at: https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/nncf . It leverages recent advances of various network compression methods and implements some of them, namely quantization, sparsity, filter pruning and binarization.

arxiv-2106-15221.title: Fact Check: Analyzing Financial Events from Multilingual News Sources
arxiv-2106-15221.creator: Linyi Yang, Tin Lok James Ng, Barry Smyth, Ruihai Dong
arxiv-2106-15221.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Linyi Yang, Tin Lok James Ng, Barry Smyth, Ruihai Dong. The explosion in the sheer magnitude and complexity of financial news data in recent years makes it increasingly challenging for investment analysts to extract valuable insights and perform analysis. We propose FactCheck in finance, a web-based news aggregator with deep learning models, to provide analysts with a holistic view of important financial events from multilingual news sources and extract events using an unsupervised clustering method.

arxiv-2208-14483.title: Multiple products of meromorphic functions
arxiv-2208-14483.creator: A. Zuevsky
arxiv-2208-14483.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. Zuevsky. Let 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} be an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra, and G G be the algebraic completion of a 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} -module. Using the geometric model of Schottky uniformization of Riemann sphere to obtain a higher genus Riemann surface, we construct a family of parametric extensions of coboundary operators for the double complexes of meromorphic functions depending on elements of G G , and having prescribed analytic properties.

arxiv-2211-03669.title: A Dixmier type averaging property of automorphisms on a C ∗ C^{*} -algebra
arxiv-2211-03669.creator: Mikael Rørdam
arxiv-2211-03669.description: Abstract In his study of the relative Dixmier property for inclusions of von Neumann algebras and of C ∗ C^{*} -algebras, Popa considered a certain property of automorphisms on C ∗ C^{*} -algebras, that we here call the strong averaging property .

arxiv-2310-03081.title: Star formation and AGN activity 500 Myr after the Big Bang: Insights from JWST
arxiv-2310-03081.creator: Jordan C. J. D’Silva, Simon P. Driver, Claudia D. P. Lagos, Aaron S. G. Robotham, Jake Summers, Rogier A. Windhorst
arxiv-2310-03081.description: Abstract We consider the effect of including an active galactic nuclei (AGN) component when fitting spectral energy distributions of 109 spectroscopically confirmed z ≈ 3.5 − 12.5 z\approx 3.5-12.5 galaxies with JWST . Remarkably, we find that the resulting cosmic star formation history is ≈ 0.4 \approx 0.4 dex lower at z ≳ 9.5 z\gtrsim 9.

arxiv-2310-13440.title: The Past, Present, and Future of Typological Databases in NLP
arxiv-2310-13440.creator: Emi BaylorMcGill UniversityMila Quebec AI Institute emily.baylor@mail.mcgill.ca, Esther PloegerDept. of Computer ScienceAalborg University espl@cs.aau.dk, Johannes BjervaDept. of Computer ScienceAalborg University jbjerva@cs.aau.dk
arxiv-2310-13440.description: Abstract Typological information has the potential to be beneficial in the development of NLP models, particularly for low-resource languages. Unfortunately, current large-scale typological databases, notably WALS and Grambank, are inconsistent both with each other and with other sources of typological information, such as linguistic grammars.

arxiv-2407-15690.title: Landauer principle and the second law in a relativistic communication scenario
arxiv-2407-15690.creator: Yuri J. Alvim, Lucas C. Céleri
arxiv-2407-15690.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuri J. Alvim, Lucas C. Céleri. The problem of formulating thermodynamics in a relativistic scenario remains unresolved, although many proposals exist in the literature. The challenge arises due to the intrinsic dynamic structure of spacetime as established by the general theory of relativity. With the discovery of the physical nature of information, which underpins Landauer’s principle, we believe that information theory should play a role in understanding this problem.

arxiv-2501-17444.title: Formally Verifying a Transformation from MLTL Formulas to Regular Expressions
arxiv-2501-17444.creator: Zili Wang, Katherine Kosaian, Kristin Yvonne Rozier
arxiv-2501-17444.description: Abstract Mission-time Linear Temporal Logic (MLTL), a widely used subset of popular specification logics like STL and MTL, is often used to model and verify real world systems in safety-critical contexts. As the results of formal verification are only as trustworthy as their input specifications, the WEST tool was created to facilitate writing MLTL specifications.

arxiv-2512-19327.title: Extended OpenTT games dataset: A table tennis dataset for fine-grained shot type and point outcome detection
arxiv-2512-19327.creator: Moamal Fadhil Abdul–Mahdi, Jonas Bruun Hubrechts, Thomas Martini Jørgensen, Emil Hovad
arxiv-2512-19327.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Moamal Fadhil Abdul–Mahdi, Jonas Bruun Hubrechts, Thomas Martini Jørgensen, Emil Hovad. Automatically detecting and classifying strokes in table tennis video can streamline training workflows, enrich broadcast overlays, and enable fine-grained performance analytics. For this to be possible, annotated video data of table tennis is needed. We extend the public OpenTTGames dataset with highly detailed, frame-accurate shot type annotations (forehand, backhand with subtypes), player posture labels (body lean and leg stance), and rally outcome tags at point end.

arxiv-2602-11950.title: Radio Map Prediction from Noisy Environment Information and Sparse Observations
arxiv-2602-11950.creator: Fabian Jaensch, Çağkan Yapar, Giuseppe Caire, Begüm Demir
arxiv-2602-11950.description: Abstract Many works have investigated radio map and path loss prediction in wireless networks using deep learning, in particular using convolutional neural networks. However, most assume perfect environment information, which is unrealistic in practice due to sensor limitations, mapping errors, and temporal changes.

arxiv-2605-08890.creator: Linsa G. J, Pushpender Singh, Rohit Dhir, M. Ameen Poyli

pmc-10626684.title: The complexities of communication at hospital discharge of older patients: a qualitative study of healthcare professionals’ views
pmc-10626684.creator: Henrik Cam, Björn Wennlöf, Ulrika Gillespie, Kristin Franzon, Elisabet I. Nielsen, Mia Ling, Karl-Johan Lindner, Thomas Gerardus Hendrik Kempen, Sofia Kälvemark Sporrong
pmc-10626684.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundHospital discharge of older patients is a high-risk situation in terms of patient safety. Due to the fragmentation of the healthcare system, communication and coordination between stakeholders are required at discharge. The aim of this study was to explore communication in general and medication information transfer in particular at hospital discharge of older patients from the perspective of healthcare professionals (HCPs) across different organisations within the healthcare system.MethodsWe conducted a qualitative study using focus group and individual or group interviews with HCPs

pmc-10709323.title: LncRNA MIR200CHG inhibits EMT in gastric cancer by stabilizing miR-200c from target-directed miRNA degradation
pmc-10709323.creator: Yixiao Zhu, Chengmei Huang, Chao Zhang, Yi Zhou, Enen Zhao, Yaxin Zhang, Xingyan Pan, Huilin Huang, Wenting Liao, Xin Wang
pmc-10709323.description: Gastric cancer (GC) is a heterogeneous disease, threatening millions of lives worldwide, yet the functional roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in different GC subtypes remain poorly characterized. Microsatellite stable (MSS)/epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) GC is the most aggressive subtype associated with a poor prognosis.

pmc-13021147.title: Coaching Teachers to Implement Equity and Social and Emotional Learning Focused Curricula in the Classroom: Insights from a Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13021147.creator: Meredith P Franco, Sandra Rouiller, Catherine P Bradshaw, Elise T Pas, Toshna Pandey, Chelsea A Kaihoi, Jessika H Bottiani
pmc-13021147.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Teacher coaching has frequently been used to support the implementation of social and emotional learning (SEL) interventions in classrooms. Though research on effective SEL implementation coaching strategies is growing, less is known about coaching to support equity-focused SEL.

pmc-13067479.title: Association between functional combined anteversion and dislocation after revision total hip arthroplasty
pmc-13067479.creator: Yuta Hieda, Hyonmin Choe, Koki Abe, Hiroyuki Ike, Masashi Shimoda, Hironori Yamane, Akira Morita, Kosuke Sumi, Ken Kumagai, Naomi Kobayashi, Yutaka Inaba
pmc-13067479.description: BackgroundDislocation is a serious complication that should be avoided in total hip arthroplasty (THA). Combined anteversion (CA) of the cup and stem is a concept for appropriate implant positioning; however, the effect of functional changes in femoral rotation has not been well investigated.

pmc-13259267.title: TailBoost: Tail-Synthetic Learning for Boosting Long-Tailed Skin Cancer Image Classification
pmc-13259267.creator: Tianyunxi Wei, Yijin Huang, Li Lin, Pujin Cheng, Xiaoying Tang
pmc-13259267.description: Skin cancer image data often exhibit long-tailed distributions due to the inherent challenges in data collection and annotation. Specifically, a few predominant classes dominate a dataset of interest, while minority classes, referred to as tail classes, are underrepresented with only limited numbers of samples. Such imbalance is highly likely to adversely affect the performance of deep learning models.

pmc-13433948.title: Design and implementation of a novel multilevel inverter for renewable energy applications
pmc-13433948.creator: C. Dhanamjayulu
pmc-13433948.description: For renewable energy applications, an optimal output with lower power electronics components requires an efficient power electronic circuit. In this paper, a novel asymmetrical thirteen-one level multilevel inverter with ideal components is suggested for use in renewable energy applications. It uses asymmetrical DC sources and fewer circuit components to produce thirteen-one output levels.

pmc-13538560.title: Evaluation of metal-oxide semiconductors for the photocatalytic degradation of chloroquine phosphate in real-world water matrices
pmc-13538560.creator: Fangyuan Zheng, Roberto Fernández de Luis, Senentxu Lanceros-Méndez, Pedro M Martins

pmc-13585542.title: Number-line estimation training in preschoolers supports early mathematical development and is associated with a stronger approximate-to-symbolic numerical pathway
pmc-13585542.creator: Maybí Morell-Ruiz, Eva-Maria Ternblad, Betty Tärning, Sonja Holmer, Magnus Haake, Agneta Gulz
pmc-13585542.description: Understanding how children connect approximate nonsymbolic magnitudes with exact symbolic numbers is a central question in theories of numerical development. A major debate concerns the directionality of this relation: whether approximate magnitude representations scaffold the acquisition of symbolic number knowledge, as proposed by mapping accounts, or whether symbolic number learning refines approximate magnitude processing, as proposed by refinement accounts.

pmc-13610981.title: Pharmacological Potential of Selenoproteins in the Regulation of Oxidative Stress in Liver Diseases
pmc-13610981.creator: Elena G. Varlamova
pmc-13610981.description: Background: Pathological activation of oxidative metabolism is a universal catalyst for liver parenchyma destruction. While physiological pools of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) regulate hepatic regeneration and cellular respiration, decompensation of endogenous antioxidant systems induces cascading damage across hepatocytes, sinusoidal endothelial cells, Kupffer macrophages, and hepatic stellate cells.
